newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian industrial group slams child labor.
newsitem.headline: Colombian industrial group slams child labor.

text.p: A leading industrial group lashed out at rampant child labour in Colombia on Wednesday and urged its members to clamp a blanket ban on the hiring of anyone under 18 years old.

Criticism of the widespread but rarely admitted practice of hiring children to work for sub-standard wages came in a directive from the powerful National Association of Industrialists (ANDI) to its 700 members across Colombia.
The directive said 2.4 million children -- or about 90 percent of all Colombians between nine and 17 years of age who live in poverty or extreme poverty -- were working instead of going to school.
By hiring them, businessmen and industrialists were effectively depriving the children, and Colombia itself, of a better future, ANDI said.

"The lack of education and technical training among children and young people prevents them from gaining access to better living and working conditions in a world that is increasingly in demand of qualified personnel," it said.
It was not immediately clear how the industrial group planned to enforce the ban on hiring minors. Colombian labour law prohibits the practice but it is commonplace nevertheless.
One of the most infamous cases of child labour in Colombia involved the longstanding use of small children to burrow into tight-fitting coal mine shafts in northwestern Antioquia province.
The Labour Ministry announced last year that mine owners had unanimously agreed to stop the practice and there has been no evidence that it continues today.
